editorial:
You meet Charles Foster Kane as a powerful newspaper boss who has just died, leaving behind a single mysterious word: Rosebud. A reporter sets out to figure out what that word meant, digging into Kane's past through interviews with people who knew him. You watch his life unfold from a poor kid taken from his mother to a rich, powerful man who slowly loses everything around him. The movie feels like a puzzle, with each person's story adding another piece to a man you never fully understand.

The acting is strong, especially Orson Welles as Kane, and the camera work still looks impressive today. The story moves at a steady pace, though some scenes feel a bit slow by modern standards. The black-and-white look and old-school style might take a little getting used to, but the mystery keeps you hooked. If you enjoy classic films, character studies, or stories about power and loneliness, this is a great pick.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Kane dies alone in his huge mansion, whispering Rosebud. Workers later burn his belongings, and you see a sled with the name Rosebud on it tossed into the fire. It turns out Rosebud was the sled Kane played with as a boy before he was taken from his mother. The twist is that all his money and power never replaced the simple happiness he lost as a child.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic films and character studies.
